matched_rules.because: Storms are active (lightning caused utility voltage swells), a portion of the datacenter transferred to generator power, and mechanical cooling shut down despite surge suppressors.

Mechanical cooling is down and the datacenter is running on its load-dependent thermal buffer; customer impact began when storage servers shut down due to unsafe temperatures, indicating the buffer was depleted and automated shutdowns started.

next_actions.action: Immediately verify that mechanical cooling systems are still running, rather than assuming surge suppressors protected them.
Treat the datacenter as being on a load-dependent thermal buffer and start planning for its depletion.
Transfer the rest of the datacenter to generators to stabilize the power supply while storms are still active.
Treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted.
Expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin.
Recognize that in parts of the datacenter temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down.

escalate.to: facility operations lead and cooling plant engineer
escalate.reason: Mechanical cooling confirmed shut down while storms remain active in the area (R-001 trigger).

not_covered: No rule addresses the specific scenario of lightning-induced voltage swells causing both a partial power transfer and a simultaneous mechanical cooling shutdown despite surge suppressors; R-001 covers the response but not the root cause or prevention.

No rule addresses the fact that customer impact began with storage server shutdowns due to unsafe temperatures; R-002 anticipates automated shutdowns but does not cover the specific sequence or storage-specific impact.
No rule addresses the adequacy of the load-dependent thermal buffer design or its depletion rate under these conditions.
No rule addresses coordination with utility power or lightning protection beyond surge suppressors.

per_finding.note: R-001 explicitly names lightning-induced voltage swells shutting down mechanical cooling despite surge suppressors.
R-002 directs treating the thermal buffer as finite and expecting automated shutdown once safe thresholds are exceeded.
R-002 next action explicitly recognizes temperatures can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before shutdown.
R-001 next action directs transferring the rest of the datacenter to generators while storms are active.
R-002 anticipates automated shutdowns but does not specify storage servers or the extent of hardware damage.
No rule addresses forensic analysis of hardware or review of recovery procedures.
No rule addresses evaluating future hardware design for storage scale unit resiliency.
